youtube.title: Why Some Toothbrushes Have Blue Bristles 🪥 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Many toothbrushes have a band of blue indicator bristles. They're dyed with a colour that slowly wears away with normal brushing. When the blue has faded about halfway down the bristles, the bristles themselves are worn and splayed and no longer clean as well, so it's time for a new brush. That usually happens after about three months, which matches dentists' advice to replace your toothbrush every three to four months.
